headline: Barclays: 76% of us say AI makes scams convincing, but only 36% check the shop
summary: A Barclays survey ahead of Black Friday found three in four UK adults think AI has made scams more convincing. Only 36% say they would check a website is genuine before buying.
body: Barclays published new research on 13 November, two weeks before Black Friday. Opinium surveyed 2,000 UK adults for the bank between 23 and 27 October. Three in four (76%) said AI has made scams more convincing. Only 36% said they would check a website is genuine before they buy, and 34% feel confident they could spot an AI-generated scam while shopping online.

Claims from younger shoppers are climbing fastest. Barclays says the value of purchase scam claims from its customers aged 18 to 29 rose 56.3% in the first half of 2026 compared with a year earlier. Across all its customers, the rise was 14.2%.
In the same survey, 44% said AI makes fake reviews harder to spot, and 43% said the same about fake retailer websites. Before you pay, check the seller, however polished the page looks.
do_this: Type the retailer’s web address yourself or use its official app. Barclays says don’t click links in texts, emails, ads or social posts.
Pay by debit card, credit card or a trusted payment service. Never pay a seller you don’t know by bank transfer.
If a countdown timer or “last chance” offer rushes you, stop and check the deal first. If you think you’ve been scammed, call your bank straight away.
